newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab businessman makes peace investment in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arab businessman makes peace investment in Israel.

text.p: Businessman Ibrahim Kamel, a rare Egyptian investor in the Israeli market, said on Thursday he had bought a stake in Israel's Koor Industries as a political gesture to promote peace.
Kamel, chairman of the Kato group of companies, told Reuters the aim was to encourage the new Israeli government towards a settlement with the Palestinians.
He said he once thought that Arab investment in Israel should wait until Israel made peace with all its neighbours -- a view shared by many Arab businessmen and governments.

"I have changed my mind, simply because I feel that moves like the one I made could make the Israeli government more able to make some of the difficult decisions that lie ahead before we arrive at a final agreement for the Palestinians," he added.
Kamel said some friends and acquaintances had phoned him for an explanation of his controversial decision but were satisfied with his explanations.

Despite 18 years of peace most Egyptians have never been enthusiastic about relations with Israel and economic relations are limited. Egyptian public opinion has grown even more hostile since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took office last June.
Kamel, who has interests in the food industry, banking, real estate and trade, declined to say how much he had invested in Koor Industries but he said it was "not substantial".
He said it was the first time his companies had bought a stake in an Israeli company.

"At this stage it is a symbol more than anything else. As good human beings we would like to encourage the Israeli government to make the necessary decisions...and show that by making progress there is always a positive feedback," he added.

Kamel, who visited Israel last month and met Netanyahu, said making peace between Israel and Syria and Lebanon would turn out to be easy compared to the current phase of Israeli-Palestinian negotiations.

"This (the Palestinian question) has been always the core of the problem...but as we see continuous progress on this part of the peace process, we will also see closer cooperation between the Egyptian and Israeli business communities," he added.
Kamel met Netanyahu again in the Swiss resort of Davos last week and the Israeli prime minister referred to Kamel's investment in a dinner speech.
